caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 608 of 1995
lawyer: For the petitioners : Mr. B. Hossian, Advocate on Record, Supreme Court. For the Respondent : Mr. Md. Aftab' Hossain, Advocate on Record, Supreme Court.
parties:
Superintendent of Police. Naogaon and others ------ Petitioners.
Versus
Sree Delip Kumar Barmon ------ Respondent.
full_judgment: Mohammad Abdur Rouf, J: Respondent Delip Kumar Barmon, a police constable while engaged on duty in the guardroom of Sonali Bank. Naogaon was found absent from duty by Mr. A. K. Ibrahim Additional Superintendent of Police on 23-4-1991 at 23.50 hours and'` again on 1-5-1991 at 11.50 hours. Accordingly departmental proceeding was initiated against him and the inquiry Officer. Mr. Golam Kibria, Assistant Superintendent of Police found him guy and recommended imposition of fine of Tk. 1080/- to be realized from his monthly salary at the rate of Tk. 45/- per month for two years. But the Superintendent of Police disagreed with the recommendation of the Inquiry Officer and removed the respondent from service by an order dated 16-6-1991. The respondent to the D. 1. G of Police was dismissed on 24-8-91. The respondent preferred another appeal to the I. G of Police which was also dismissed on 21-11-91. The respondent then filed Administrative. This question was raised before the Administrative Tribunal and Issue No. 1 was also framed as to whether the case is barred by limitation?' The tribunal on consideration of the materials on record held that the case was within 6 months from the date of disposal of the appeal by the I. G. of Police. Hence it was not barred by limitation. No cross-appeal on this finding was preferred by the pre-sent petitioners. It does not appear from the impugned judgment that the question of limitation as raised by the petitioners before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal. Now it cannot be raised. Thus we do not find any cogent reason to interfere with the impugned judgment and order. The delay is condoned, but the petition is dismissed.
